name: Chicken of the Woods

facts.what: The tender edges of the young bracket, always cooked
facts.where: On oaks and other hardwoods, never on the ground

caution: Always cook it, and eat a small amount your first time: some people react even to correctly-identified chicken of the woods, and specimens on conifers or certain oaks disagree with more people. Mushrooms demand expert confirmation. Never eat a wild plant on this guide's word alone. Confirm identity against several sources and learn the look-alikes first.

sections.title: Identification
sections.body: Overlapping shelves of vivid sulphur-yellow and orange growing straight from a tree trunk or log. No gills, a pore surface underneath.

sections.title: In the kitchen
sections.body: The young tender edges really do echo chicken. Take only the soft growing margin, cook it fully, and try a little the first time.
